title: The 5 Biggest Diamonds Ever Mined, Ranked (4 Came From One Mine)

scenes.text: The five biggest diamonds ever mined. Four came from one mine, all since 2019.

scenes.label: Karowe stone · 1,476 ct
scenes.text: Number five: an unnamed 1,476-carat stone, found at Botswana's Karowe mine in 2025.

scenes.label: Sewelô · 1,758 ct
scenes.text: Number four: the Sewelô. 1,758 carats, same mine, 2019. Louis Vuitton bought it.

scenes.label: Karowe stone · 2,036 ct
scenes.text: Number three: 2,036 carats. Karowe again, found in 2025.

scenes.label: Motswedi · ~2,490 ct
scenes.text: Number two: the Motswedi, 2024. About 2,490 carats, nearly half a kilogram. Karowe, of course.

scenes.label: Cullinan · 3,106 ct
scenes.text: Number one: the Cullinan, South Africa, 1905. 3,106 carats. Unbeaten for 120 years, and its biggest pieces sit in the British Crown Jewels.

description:
The five biggest diamonds ever mined, ranked by their rough weight in carats.
The Cullinan (3,106 carats, Premier Mine, South Africa, 1905) is still the largest; stones cut from it are in the British Crown Jewels. The next four all came from Lucara's Karowe mine in Botswana: the Motswedi (reported as 2,492 carats when found in 2024, 2,488 when examined by the GIA), a 2,036-carat stone (2025), the 1,758-carat Sewelô (2019) and a 1,476-carat stone (2025). The Sergio, a 3,167-carat black carbonado found at the surface in Brazil in 1895, is heavier but is not gem diamond and is usually listed apart.
Would you cut number one, or keep it whole?
first_comment: Four of the top five came out of one mine in six years. Which stone would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
